entries.content:
Strix, the open-source AI penetration testing tool, can now run on any of the 400+ models on Vercel AI Gateway.

Strix can reach models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM, Deepseek, and others through a single API with no markup, removing the need to sign up for multiple providers. Usage and cost are tracked across all models in AI Gateway.

Strix selects the Gateway through 

STRIX_LLM
, where the model is the standard AI Gateway 
/
ID behind a 
vercel_ai_gateway/
prefix:

terminal

      
export STRIX_LLM="vercel_ai_gateway/zai/glm-5.3"export LLM_API_KEY="your-ai-gateway-api-key"

See Strix's AI Gateway setup guide to configure it and get started today.

entries.content:
IP geolocation on Vercel now resolves visitor locations with finer network granularity, delivering city-level data for nearly all requests and postal-code data for 90% of traffic.

Geolocation data is now refreshed more often, so locations keep up as IP ranges are reassigned and routing changes. This is enabled for all projects with no code or configuration changes required. Existing geolocation headers along with the 

geolocation()
helper in 

@vercel/functions
, return the same fields for Vercel Functions and Routing Middleware.

If you use geolocation for access controls, localization, or compliance, some visitors will now resolve to a different city or country, most often traffic from VPNs, hosting providers, and leased IP ranges:

  • Physical termination location:

    Subnets announced from a hosting provider in a different country than their regional internet registry (RIR) record now resolve to the data center where the traffic actually terminates.

  • Testing geo-dependent routes:

    Verify access rules against an IP's active network location rather than its static registry allocation.

Read the request headers documentation for all available geolocation headers and fields.

entries.title: Vercel Flags starts 7x faster and no longer extends function duration

entries.content:
On Vercel, the Vercel Flags SDK now initializes faster on cold starts, and usage reporting no longer keeps functions running after the response.

Copy link to headingFaster cold starts

Two changes speed up SDK initialization on cold starts:

  • The SDK loads and parses the flags datafile bundled with your deployment as soon as the client is created, so it’s ready before your code evaluates its first flag.

  • Every function invocation now includes the current datafile revision, so the SDK can check whether the bundled datafile is up to date without a network request.

In internal testing, eliminating the network wait reduced p75 cold-start SDK initialization time from over 70 ms to 10 ms, roughly 7x faster.

After initialization, flag reads are effectively instant. Across cold and warm invocations, p99 flag-read latency is under 1 ms.

Copy link to headingUsage reporting no longer extends function duration

The SDK previously used 

waitUntil
for usage reporting, keeping functions running after the response was sent. It now passes usage events to the Vercel runtime, so reporting no longer adds to function duration.

Update 

@flags-sdk/vercel
to version 1.5.3 or later and redeploy your application: 
      
pnpm add @flags-sdk/vercel@latest

Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation.

entries.content:
The fx adapter for the AI SDK’s 

HarnessAgent
now uses 
libfx
, the TypeScript library for fx. The harness and model requests run in your application’s process, while built-in filesystem and shell operations remain isolated in the sandbox.

This simplifies sandbox setup: you no longer need to install fx inside the sandbox, run a sandbox bridge, or expose a sandbox port. Model credentials stay on the host, outside the environment where the agent runs commands.

The rewrite also adds:

  • Built-in tool filtering: choose which built-in tools the agent can use

  • Mid-turn steering: send new instructions while a turn is running

  • Structured output: generate responses that match a schema

  • Image tool results: return images to the model through 

    toModelOutput()

Sessions can be saved and resumed in a new host process.

Update 

@ai-sdk/harness-fx
to the latest version to use the new adapter. Learn more in the fx harness documentation.

This can reduce latency when your functions call APIs or databases over HTTP.Temporal API offers an alternative to Date with immutable values and built-in time zone and calendar suppor
entries.content:
Node.js 26 LTS is now Generally Available for builds and Vercel Functions.

This release includes:

  • HTTP/2 by default for built-in 

    fetch
    (Undici 8) lets multiple requests share a connection with servers that support it. This can reduce latency when your functions call APIs or databases over HTTP.

  • Temporal API offers an alternative to 

    Date
    with immutable values and built-in time zone and calendar support.

  • V8 version 14.6, the updated JavaScript engine, adds features such as 

    Map.prototype.getOrInsert()
    to retrieve an existing value or insert a default when a key is missing.

Copy link to headingUsing Node.js 26

Node.js 26 is the default for all new projects.

  • Automatic upgrades: If 

    engines.node
    in your existing project’s 
    package.json
    allows 26, such as 
    >=20
    , your Node.js builds on Vercel will use 26 on the next deployment.

  • Manual upgrades: Set 

    engines.node
    to 
    26.x
    in your project's 
    package.json
    and redeploy.

  • Prebuilt deployments: Use Vercel CLI version 65.8.0 or later to deploy Node.js 26 Functions.

  • HTTP/1.1 in Functions: To keep HTTP/1.1, set the 

    VERCEL_FETCH_DISABLE_H2
    environment variable to 

    1
    and redeploy.

Minor and patch updates to Node.js 26 roll out automatically for builds and Vercel Functions.

Read the Node.js version documentation to learn more.

entries.title: Vercel Connect adds webhook triggers for more providers
entries.summary: Vercel Connect now supports webhook triggers for Resend, X, Twilio, Notion, and Telegram.Connect receives webhook events, such as Telegram bot messages or emails received by your Resend domain, and forwards them to an endpoint in your Vercel project. It verifies incoming requests and handles provider heartbeats and verification challenges for you.To get started:Open Vercel Connect in the dashboard
entries.content:
Vercel Connect now supports webhook triggers for Resend, X, Twilio, Notion, and Telegram.

Connect receives webhook events, such as Telegram bot messages or emails received by your Resend domain, and forwards them to an endpoint in your Vercel project. It verifies incoming requests and handles provider heartbeats and verification challenges for you.

To get started:

  • Open Vercel Connect in the dashboard. Enable triggers when creating a connector for your provider or in an existing connector’s settings. Connect registers webhooks automatically for Resend and Telegram.

  • For Twilio, Notion, and X, use the webhook URL from Connect and follow its instructions to complete setup in the provider’s settings.

  • Add a trigger destination to choose the project and endpoint that should receive events.

You can turn triggers on or off later in the connector’s settings.

In the connector’s Observability tab, select Live to watch incoming trigger events.

These connectors join existing trigger support for Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, and Linear.

Learn more in the Connect triggers documentation.

entries.title: Control AI crawlers and assistants separately in Vercel Firewall
entries.summary: You can now log or block requests from AI crawlers and AI assistants separately with the AI Bots managed ruleset in Vercel Firewall.AI crawlers: bots that collect content for indexing and model trainingAI assistants: bots that fetch pages in response to user actions or search queriesFor example, you can block AI crawlers while allowing AI assistants to retrieve your content to answer users’ questi
entries.content:
You can now log or block requests from AI crawlers and AI assistants separately with the AI Bots managed ruleset in Vercel Firewall.

  • AI crawlers: bots that collect content for indexing and model training

  • AI assistants: bots that fetch pages in response to user actions or search queries

For example, you can block AI crawlers while allowing AI assistants to retrieve your content to answer users’ questions. Vercel updates the rules as new bots are added.

To configure these controls, open your project’s Security > Firewall > Rules. Under Bot Management, enable AI Bots and select the gear icon beside it. Set an action for AI crawlers and AI assistants, then review and publish your changes.

You can also modify these rule settings using the Vercel CLI:

      
vercel firewall rules edit ai-bots --category ai-crawlers --action deny --yesvercel firewall rules edit ai-bots --category ai-assistants --action log --yes

Configure the AI Bots ruleset to block AI crawlers and allow AI assistants.

Review the changes with 

vercel firewall diff
, then apply them with 
vercel firewall publish
.

The AI Bots managed ruleset is available on all plans. Learn more in the documentation.

Contributors

Sage Abraham

The release also improves spreadsheet creation and editing, web research, and resistance to prompt inject
entries.content:
Mistral Large 4 from Mistral now uses updated weights on AI Gateway, with lower pricing for input, cached input, and output tokens.

According to Mistral’s release announcement, the updated weights improve agentic coding and defensive cybersecurity, with greater token efficiency on coding tasks. The release also improves spreadsheet creation and editing, web research, and resistance to prompt injection.

If you were already using 

mistral/mistral-large-4
via AI Gateway, there is no need to change your model to start using the updated version. The existing model ID string uses the new model with updated weights and pricing. 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'mistral/mistral-large-4',  prompt: 'Suggest three fixes for a flaky API retry loop.',});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To use Mistral Large 4 in fx, Pi, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or other harnesses, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

mistral/mistral-large-4
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

You can also try Mistral Large 4 in the model playground.

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.

AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.

You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.

entries.content:
You can now run CI for your Turborepo with one line of configuration.

      
{  "tasks": {    "lint": {      "tags": ["ci"]    }  }}

Use tags to make a task run in Vercel CI.

In Vercel's internal repositories, our wait time from 

git push
to "CI passed" is 2-6x shorter, dramatically improving our CI's ability to keep up with our coding agents.

To get started, prompt your agent in your repo:

Set up Vercel CI for this repository. Run `npx skills use vercel/ci@setup` and follow the skill's instructions to select initial tasks, configure Vercel CI, and open a pull request.

Each task marked with a 

ci
tag runs on every push. Vercel CI automatically takes care of:

  • Only running CI that is affected by your code changes

  • Task caching with Vercel Remote Cache

  • Installing dependencies once per run

  • Caching dependencies across code updates

To learn more:
